A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OTA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original OTA evaluations, value-function diagnostics, and ablations on OGBench, including detailed results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds n-step HIQL comparisons, matched-hyperparameter experiments, and visual-play evaluations.

M1.justification: The option construction, OTA objective in Equation (4), and hierarchical policy objectives remain unchanged. The added n-step implementation is a comparison variant of HIQL.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds play datasets for Visual-cube-double, Visual-cube-triple, and Visual-scene alongside the retained noisy datasets. This extends data coverage within existing visual manipulation tasks; the maze coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds HIQL using n-step TD with the original discount factor. Standard HIQL, discount-adjusted HIQL, and OTA remain, and the six main benchmark baselines are unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments control hyperparameters between HIQL and OTA: Appendix D.2 uses shared maze settings, and D.3 fixes k=10 and both inverse temperatures at 3, with OTA n=2. These are additional protocols; existing training budgets and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Two substantive controls expand the mechanism analysis. Section 6.5 tests whether n-step backups alone reproduce OTA's benefits, while Appendix D.2 tests whether gains persist with matched HIQL hyperparameters. These address alternative explanations beyond v1's existing discount-scaling and abstraction-factor analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging across eight seeds and use five trajectories per environment for the consistency comparison. The existing uncertainty notation is retained, with no new significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The result set expands through n-step HIQL outcomes in Table 1 and new controlled maze and visual-play comparisons in Tables 7–8. For example, Table 7 reports OTA 91±1 versus HIQL 12±4 on HumanoidMaze-giant-navigate; Table 8 reports 28±1 versus 21±5 on Visual-cube-triple-play. Original results remain unchanged; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly assumes deterministic dynamics in Section 3 and Definition 4.1, narrowing the formal setting left implicit in v1. The existing equations and mathematical relationships otherwise remain; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diagnosing HIQL's high-level value errors, proposing option-aware temporal abstraction, and improving long-horizon goal-reaching. New experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains how exponentiated advantage weights amplify sign errors, discusses n-step target discounting and possible discount retuning, and attributes matched-hyperparameter gains to temporal abstraction. It also explicitly limits the setting to deterministic dynamics. Appendix A's original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an OTA code-access link. Appendix B.2.3 newly discloses moving-average smoothing of value estimates, although its window is unspecified. This disclosure does not establish that the procedure changed. New experiments also provide their hyperparameter settings.

R1.justification: Section 5 newly positions OTA against standard n-step TD, emphasizing the different discounting and tuning requirements. The existing positioning relative to HIQL, options, and quasimetric learning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the main text, clarifies terminology through footnotes, expands Section 6.5, and divides Appendix D into three subsections. Author information, venue text, and acknowledgments are updated, while the overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains n-step columns and abbreviated dataset labels; Tables 7–8 are added. Figure 3 receives small label and layout edits, and Figure 6 moves to another page. Existing empirical plots and appendix displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The n-step and matched-hyperparameter controls address previously untested explanations for OTA's gains, strengthening the empirical case. Explicit assumptions, smoothing disclosure, and a code pointer also improve transparency. The gains are qualified by incomplete smoothing details and Appendix D.2's claim of consistent outperformance despite a tied mean in Table 7.
